mainTopic: An egg laid on יום טוב: מוקצה and נולד, and רב נחמן's alignment of בית שמאי and בית הלל with רבי שמעון and רבי יהודה.
overview: The משנה lists cases where, unusually, בית שמאי are lenient and בית הלל are strict. These are an egg laid on יום טוב, the amounts of שאור and חמץ on פסח, and covering the blood after slaughtering on יום טוב. The גמרא first asks what kind of hen laid the egg, and concludes it must be a hen kept for laying eggs, so the egg is מוקצה. That raises the question of why בית שמאי permit it, especially since the egg is also נולד. רב נחמן answers that whoever holds of מוקצה also holds of נולד: בית שמאי follow רבי שמעון (lenient) and בית הלל follow רבי יהודה (strict). The גמרא challenges him, because on a משנה about bones and shells on שבת he placed בית הלל with רבי שמעון. The answer is that on שבת a סתם משנה follows רבי שמעון, so he matched בית הלל to it there. The explanation of why יום טוב is different continues on the next amud.

steps.title: An egg laid on יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: The משנה records a dispute about eating an egg that was laid on יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: An egg that was laid on יום טוב: בית שמאי say it may be eaten, and בית הלל say it may not be eaten.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה opens with the main case of the מסכת: may you eat an egg that came out of the hen today, on יום טוב?
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית שמאי allow the egg that same day. בית הלל forbid it. The משנה does not give reasons, so the גמרא will have to figure out what is bothering בית הלל.

keyTerms.meaning: egg
that was born / laid
Festival day
it may be eaten

steps.confusionAlert: Usually בית שמאי are the strict ones. Here it is the other way around, and that is exactly why the משנה goes on to collect other cases like this.
steps.whyThisMatters: This case gives the whole מסכת its name, and the גמרא's analysis of it shapes many later laws of יום טוב.

phrases.english: An egg that was laid on a Festival,
Beit Shammai say: it may be eaten,
and Beit Hillel say: it may not be eaten.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: בית שמאי permit eating an egg laid on יום טוב; בית הלל forbid it.

steps.title: Minimum amounts of leaven and leavened bread
steps.stepSummary: A second dispute where בית שמאי are lenient: the minimum amounts of שאור and חמץ on פסח. The גמרא later (7b) explains that this refers to the obligation to remove it (ביעור); for eating, everyone agrees the amount is a כזית.
steps.simpleTranslation: בית שמאי say: for שאור the amount is a כזית, and for חמץ the amount is a ככותבת. בית הלל say: for both, the amount is a כזית.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds another case where בית שמאי are more lenient, this time about the size that makes leaven forbidden on פסח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שאור is a very sour starter dough used to make other dough rise. חמץ is regular leavened bread. בית שמאי say regular חמץ needs the larger amount, a date-size (ככותבת). בית הלל say both need only an olive-size (כזית), which is the stricter view.

keyTerms.meaning: sourdough starter, a strong leavening agent
leavened bread
the size of an olive
the size of a large date (bigger than a כזית)
this and that, i.e., both

steps.confusionAlert: Do not wonder why a פסח law appears in a מסכת about יום טוב. It is listed here only because it is another case where בית שמאי are lenient.

phrases.english: Beit Shammai say:
leaven is in the measure of an olive-bulk,
and leavened bread in the measure of a date-bulk,

phrases.aramaic: וּבֵית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים: זֶה וְזֶה בְּכַזַּיִת.
phrases.english: and Beit Hillel say: this and that are both in the measure of an olive-bulk.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: בית שמאי: שאור is a כזית and חמץ is a ככותבת; בית הלל: both are a כזית.

steps.title: Slaughtering a wild animal or bird on יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: A third dispute: may you slaughter on יום טוב when you will have to dig up earth to cover the blood?
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone slaughters a wild animal or a bird on יום טוב, בית שמאי say he may dig with a shovel and cover the blood. בית הלל say he may not slaughter at all unless he already had earth prepared from before יום טוב.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה brings another case where בית שמאי are lenient, this time about the מצוה of כיסוי הדם on יום טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Covering the blood requires earth, and digging up fresh earth is normally a problem on יום טוב. בית שמאי allow digging from the start. בית הלל say you should only slaughter if earth was set aside before יום טוב began.

keyTerms.meaning: a wild animal and a bird (their blood must be covered)
a shovel or digging tool
and he covers (the blood)
prepared
while it was still day, before יום טוב began

phrases.english: One who slaughters a wild animal or a bird on a Festival,
Beit Shammai say:
he digs with a shovel and covers,
and Beit Hillel say: he may not slaughter
unless he had
earth prepared while it was still day.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: בית שמאי allow digging to cover the blood; בית הלל forbid slaughtering unless earth was prepared before יום טוב.

steps.title: בית הלל's concession after the fact
steps.stepSummary: בית הלל agree that if the slaughter already happened, he digs and covers, and that stove ash counts as prepared.
steps.simpleTranslation: They agree that if he already slaughtered, he should dig with a shovel and cover the blood, and that ash from a stove counts as prepared.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה limits בית הלל's strictness. They forbid slaughtering only before the fact. Once the animal is already slaughtered, the blood must be covered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So the dispute is only about what to do from the start (לכתחילה). After the fact, even בית הלל allow digging. The משנה also says that ash in a stove counts as already prepared, so it may be used. The גמרא will explain this point later.

keyTerms.meaning: and they agree / concede
that if he already slaughtered
ash of a stove

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה gives three cases of בית שמאי being lenient: the egg, the amounts of שאור and חמץ, and covering the blood. In the last case, בית הלל are strict only before the fact.

phrases.english: And they agree that if he slaughtered,
that he should dig with a shovel and cover —
that the ash of a stove is prepared.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: Once he has slaughtered, even בית הלל allow digging to cover the blood; stove ash counts as prepared.

steps.title: Which case is the משנה talking about?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what kind of situation the egg case in the משנה refers to.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: What case are we dealing with?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins by asking what kind of hen laid the egg. This question sets up the next moves.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reason an egg might be forbidden depends on what the owner planned to do with the hen. So the גמרא must first define the case before it can explain בית הלל.

keyTerms.meaning: the Talmud's discussion of the משנה
with what case are we dealing?

phrases.english: GEMARA:
With what are we dealing?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from the משנה to the גמרא's analysis of the first case.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What kind of hen laid the egg in the משנה's case?

steps.title: A hen meant for eating cannot be the case
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the idea that the משנה means a hen meant for eating, because its egg would simply be food.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say the case is a hen meant for eating, what is בית הלל's reason? It is just food that separated off!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries the first possibility, a hen the owner plans to eat, and shows right away that it does not work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the hen itself may be slaughtered and eaten on יום טוב, then the egg is just a piece of permitted food that came out of it. There would be no reason for בית הלל to forbid it, so this cannot be the משנה's case.

keyTerms.meaning: if you say (introduces a suggestion about to be rejected)
designated for eating
what is their reason?
food that has separated off

phrases.english: If we say it is about a chicken
that is designated for eating,
what is the reason of Beit Hillel?
It is food that has separated!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the first possible answer to the question of which case the משנה means.
steps.kashyaTarget: The possibility that the משנה refers to a hen designated for eating.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An egg from a permitted, edible hen is just separated food, so בית הלל would have no reason to forbid it.

steps.title: The case is a hen kept for laying eggs
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that the משנה must mean a hen kept for laying eggs.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is about a hen kept for raising eggs.
steps.whatsHappening: Since the first option failed, the גמרא proposes the other kind of hen: one the owner keeps for its eggs, not to eat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A hen kept for laying is not meant to be eaten on יום טוב, so it is מוקצה. The egg would then share the hen's מוקצה status, and that would explain why בית הלל forbid it. This is only a first answer, and the גמרא will keep examining it.

keyTerms.meaning: rather (introduces the corrected answer)
to raise / produce eggs
set aside, not usable on שבת or יום טוב

steps.whatToRemember: The גמרא sets the case as a hen kept for laying eggs. That makes the egg potentially מוקצה, which would explain why בית הלל forbid it.

phrases.english: Rather, it is about a chicken
that is designated for raising eggs.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected case (a hen for eating) with a new case definition.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משנה refers to a hen designated for laying eggs, which is מוקצה, so its egg is also forbidden according to בית הלל.

steps.title: If the egg is set aside, why do בית שמאי permit it?
steps.stepSummary: Since the egg comes from a hen kept for laying, it is מוקצה. So why do בית שמאי allow eating it on יום טוב?
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason of בית שמאי? It is מוקצה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a problem with what it just concluded. A hen kept for laying is not meant to be eaten, so her egg should be off-limits on יום טוב. Yet בית שמאי permit it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 7 the גמרא said the hen is kept for eggs, not for eating. That makes the egg something the owner did not plan to use on יום טוב, which is מוקצה. That fits בית הלל, who forbid the egg, but it seems to contradict בית שמאי, who permit it.

keyTerms.meaning: What is their reason?
Something set aside and not meant for use on שבת or יום טוב, so it is forbidden to use or move

phrases.english: What is the reason of Beit Shammai?
phrases.notes: Why do they permit eating the egg?

phrases.english: It is muktze!
phrases.notes: The egg of a hen kept for laying is set aside from use.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the result of step 7 from בית שמאי's side.
steps.kashyaTarget: בית שמאי's ruling that the egg may be eaten
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A hen kept for laying makes its egg מוקצה, and מוקצה should be forbidden.

steps.title: Maybe בית שמאי do not hold of מוקצה at all
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions the question itself. Maybe בית שמאי simply do not accept the rule of מוקצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is the difficulty? Perhaps בית שמאי do not hold of מוקצה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on its own question. It suggests there is no problem, because בית שמאי may simply disagree with the rule of מוקצה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Not every תנא holds of this kind of מוקצה, so בית שמאי could be among those who are lenient. If so, that would be the whole point of their argument with בית הלל, and step 8's question would fall away.

keyTerms.meaning: And what is the difficulty? (meaning: why is this a problem?)
Perhaps
They do not hold of it

phrases.english: And what is the difficulty?

phrases.aramaic: דִּלְמָא בֵּית שַׁמַּאי לֵית לְהוּ מוּקְצֶה!
phrases.english: Perhaps Beit Shammai do not hold of muktze!
phrases.notes: This would make their dispute with בית הלל a dispute about מוקצה.

steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The question assumes בית שמאי accept מוקצה, but they might not.

steps.title: Even those lenient on מוקצה forbid something newly created (נולד)
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains why it asked. It assumed that even those lenient on מוקצה are strict on נולד, and the egg is נולד. So the question about בית שמאי returns.
steps.simpleTranslation: We had assumed that even someone who permits מוקצה forbids נולד. So what is the reason of בית שמאי?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends its original question. It explains the assumption behind it, and then asks the same question again.
steps.deeperAnalysis: נולד is something that came into existence on שבת or יום טוב. An egg laid on יום טוב is a clear example. If even those lenient on מוקצה forbid נולד, then saying "בית שמאי don't hold of מוקצה" does not help, and the question stands again.

keyTerms.meaning: It entered our mind (we had assumed)
Something that came into being on שבת or יום טוב
Permits / forbids

steps.confusionAlert: מוקצה and נולד are two separate categories. Here the גמרא assumes they can be split, so someone could be lenient on one and strict on the other. רב נחמן will reject that assumption in the next step.

phrases.english: It entered our mind (we assumed):
even one who permits muktze
forbids nolad (something newly created).
phrases.notes: An egg laid on יום טוב is נולד.

phrases.english: So what is the reason of Beit Shammai?
phrases.notes: The גמרא repeats the question from step 8 because its basis has now been explained.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the rejection in step 9 and brings back the question from step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: בית שמאי's ruling that the egg is permitted
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Even if בית שמאי are lenient on מוקצה, the egg is נולד, and נולד is forbidden even by those lenient on מוקצה.

steps.title: רב נחמן: מוקצה and נולד go together
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן keeps the case as a hen kept for laying. He explains that whoever holds of מוקצה also holds of נולד, and whoever doesn't, doesn't. So בית שמאי follow רבי שמעון and בית הלל follow רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: The case really is a hen kept for laying eggs. Whoever holds of מוקצה also holds of נולד, and whoever does not hold of מוקצה does not hold of נולד. בית שמאי follow רבי שמעון, and בית הלל follow רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן answers the question by rejecting the assumption from step 10. מוקצה and נולד are a package deal, so being lenient on one means being lenient on the other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once מוקצה and נולד go together, בית שמאי can be lenient on both, like רבי שמעון, and permit the egg. בית הלל are strict on both, like רבי יהודה, and forbid it. The case stays a hen kept for laying, as step 7 concluded.

keyTerms.meaning: Actually / really (we keep our earlier explanation)
A hen kept for laying eggs

steps.whatToRemember: According to רב נחמן, whoever holds of מוקצה holds of נולד, and whoever doesn't, doesn't. בית שמאי follow רבי שמעון (lenient), and בית הלל follow רבי יהודה (strict).
steps.whyThisMatters: This links the egg dispute to the larger argument between רבי שמעון and רבי יהודה about מוקצה. It is the base for the challenges that follow.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said: Actually
it is about a hen kept for laying eggs,
and whoever holds of muktze
also holds of nolad,
and whoever does not hold of muktze
does not hold of nolad.
Beit Shammai follow Rabbi Shimon,
and Beit Hillel follow Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 10 by rejecting its assumption.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rejects the assumption behind the question
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Even those lenient on מוקצה are strict on נולד, so בית שמאי have no reason to permit the egg.
steps.terutzMaskana: מוקצה and נולד go together. בית שמאי are lenient on both, like רבי שמעון, so they permit the egg.

steps.title: Did רב נחמן really say this? A משנה about bones and shells
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא doubts that רב נחמן said בית הלל follow רבי יהודה. It quotes a משנה where בית הלל forbid lifting bones and shells off a table on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Did רב נחמן really say this? But we learned in a משנה: בית שמאי say one may lift bones and shells off the table, and בית הלל say one removes the whole board and shakes it off.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a challenge against רב נחמן by quoting a משנה from מסכת שבת. This step sets up the challenge, and the next step completes it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this משנה, בית הלל do not let you pick up the bones and shells themselves, because they are מוקצה. You may only move the board, which is a usable vessel. That matches בית הלל being strict on מוקצה. The גמרא will soon show how this conflicts with something else רב נחמן said.

keyTerms.meaning: Did he really say so? (introduces a challenge)
Bones and shells (leftovers that are not food)
A board or tray used as the table surface

phrases.english: And did Rav Nachman really say this?
But didn't we learn in a mishna:
Beit Shammai say:
one may lift bones and shells off the table,
and Beit Hillel say:
one removes the entire board and shakes it off.
phrases.notes: You move the board, which is allowed, and not the bones themselves.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן הָכִי? וְהָתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a challenge against רב נחמן's answer in step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's claim that בית הלל follow רבי יהודה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה shows בית הלל's view on מוקצה. Step 13 compares it with another statement of רב נחמן to show a contradiction.

steps.title: רב נחמן elsewhere says בית הלל follow רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes its challenge from step 12. On the bones-and-shells משנה, רב נחמן reversed the opinions so that בית שמאי follow רבי יהודה and בית הלל follow רבי שמעון. That contradicts what he said about the egg.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב נחמן said: We only have it this way: בית שמאי follow רבי יהודה, and בית הלל follow רבי שמעון!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא completes the question it started in step 12. It quotes רב נחמן himself, who said that in the bones-and-shells משנה the opinions must be flipped so that בית הלל follow רבי שמעון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 11, רב נחמן said בית הלל follow רבי יהודה, who holds of מוקצה. Here he says the reverse: בית הלל follow רבי שמעון, who does not hold of מוקצה. The same אמורא cannot seem to hold both, so this is a direct contradiction between his two statements.

keyTerms.meaning: We have nothing but this (version). רב נחמן is saying the opinions must be read in reverse.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two cases. In the egg case (step 11), רב נחמן put בית הלל with רבי יהודה. In the bones-and-shells case on שבת, he put בית הלל with רבי שמעון. The contradiction is between these two statements of the same person.

phrases.english: And Rav Nachman said:
phrases.notes: This is said about the bones-and-shells משנה quoted in step 12.

phrases.english: We have nothing other than (this version):
phrases.notes: He is reversing the opinions as printed in that משנה.

phrases.english: Beit Shammai hold like Rabbi Yehuda,
phrases.notes: In other words, בית שמאי hold of מוקצה.

phrases.english: and Beit Hillel hold like Rabbi Shimon!
phrases.notes: In other words, בית הלל do not hold of מוקצה. This is the opposite of step 11.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַב נַחְמָן: אָנוּ אֵין לָנוּ אֶלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the challenge begun in step 12 by quoting רב נחמן's reversal of that משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's statement in step 11 that בית הלל follow רבי יהודה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Contradiction: רב נחמן himself elsewhere places בית הלל with רבי שמעון.

steps.title: On שבת the unattributed משנה follows רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן would answer that his reversal applies only to שבת. An unattributed משנה about שבת follows רבי שמעון, so he lined בית הלל up with רבי שמעון there. The word 'אבל' opens the contrast with יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן would tell you: Regarding שבת, the תנא taught us an unattributed משנה that follows רבי שמעון. As we learned: 'We may cut up pumpkins in front of an animal, and a dead animal in front of dogs.' So he sets בית הלל to follow רבי שמעון. But...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers for רב נחמן. His reversal was only about שבת, because a plain, unattributed משנה about שבת follows רבי שמעון. The last word, 'אבל' ('But'), sets up the next move, which explains why יום טוב is different.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה in שבת allows cutting up a dead animal for dogs, even though it might seem מוקצה. That matches רבי שמעון, who does not hold of מוקצה. The הלכה generally follows an unattributed משנה, and it also follows בית הלל, so רב נחמן made them match on שבת. This leaves room for him to say בית הלל follow רבי יהודה when the topic is יום טוב.

keyTerms.meaning: He would say to you. This introduces an answer given on someone's behalf.
The תנא taught us an unattributed (סתם) משנה. The הלכה usually follows such a משנה.
We may cut up pumpkins (to make them easier for the animal to eat).
An animal that died without שחיטה. Here it may be cut up for dogs on שבת.
He establishes, meaning he interprets the opinion this way.

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that רב נחמן's approach depends on the topic. For שבת, he aligns בית הלל with the unattributed משנה that follows רבי שמעון. For יום טוב, a different reasoning will apply.
steps.confusionAlert: The step is not finished. 'אבל' at the end means the reason for יום טוב is still coming on the next amud.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman would say to you:
phrases.notes: This is the answer to the contradiction.

phrases.english: Regarding Shabbat,
phrases.notes: This limits the reversal to the topic of שבת.

phrases.english: where the Tanna taught us an unattributed Mishnah following Rabbi Shimon,
phrases.notes: The הלכה usually follows a סתם משנה.

phrases.english: as we learned: We may cut up pumpkins
in front of an animal,
and a dead animal in front of dogs.
phrases.notes: This is allowed even though it might seem מוקצה, which matches רבי שמעון.

phrases.aramaic: מוֹקֵים לָהּ לְבֵית הִלֵּל כְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן.
phrases.english: So he sets Beit Hillel to follow Rabbi Shimon.
phrases.notes: This way בית הלל match the unattributed משנה.

phrases.english: But...
phrases.notes: This opens the contrast with יום טוב, which continues on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לְךָ רַב נַחְמָן: גַּבֵּי שַׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction in step 13 by limiting רב נחמן's reversal to שבת.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing contexts: שבת versus יום טוב.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב נחמן holds one fixed view about בית הלל and מוקצה everywhere, so his two statements contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: On שבת, he aligns בית הלל with רבי שמעון because a סתם משנה follows רבי שמעון. For יום טוב, a different reason (still to come) lets בית הלל follow רבי יהודה.
